# STD-014 Edition 3 - applicability FAQ (RA, July 2026)

**Is near-patient testing the same as self-testing?** No. Near-patient testing is performed by health professionals
outside a laboratory. Self-testing is performed by lay persons. A professional point-of-care device takes S25 and
does not take S08 or S26.

**Does a concept document make a section applicable?** No. Applicability follows the device being filed. Drafts for
a possible future variant do not bring S08 or S26 into the file.

**Which sections depend on class?** S28 (class D only) and S30 (class C and D since Edition 3).

**What if a section is applicable but has no approved document?** It stays in the ToC as a Gap with "None in force";
it is never marked Not applicable to hide the gap.

CAPA-0912 - Post-market surveillance plan: approval withdrawn
Opened 2026-11-11 by R. Montoya (QA Manager). Product: Kestrel-3. Document: DOC-1200 Post-market Surveillance Plan, Rev A (released 2026-09-30 under CHG0040990, 22 pages).
Finding: the plan sets no quantitative trend thresholds for field-safety signals (complaint rate per 10,000 cartridges, serious incident trend). The NB pre-submission review of 29 October flagged the same point.
Action 1 (done 2026-11-11): QA withdraws the approval of Rev A. Recorded in the Kestrel-3 Document Control Register as 'Approval withdrawn'. The signed approval envelope and the change request remain as audit trail only.
Action 2 (due 2026-11-30): draft Rev B with thresholds; route for approval; release under change control.
Consequence for submissions: until Rev B is approved there is no PMS plan in force for Kestrel-3. Rev A must not be cited as in force.

# Clinical performance study KS3-CPS-01 - status 30 October 2026 (L. Brauer)

Sites: Leiden UMC (closed), Gdansk University Hospital (closed), Aarhus Regional (enrolment complete, data cleaning).
Enrolled: 1,284 of 1,300. Database lock: planned 9 December 2026.

The report DOC-1120 exists only as a working draft (Rev A, 74 pp, six placeholders for the Aarhus data and the final
statistics). An early-release change request (CHG0041004) was cancelled on 2 November: a draft cannot be released.
For the November ToC the clinical performance study report is therefore a gap; the performance evaluation report
(DOC-1121 Rev B) summarises the interim data.

# Kestrel-3 - device summary for the technical file (RA, 2026-11-02)

**Product.** Kestrel-3 point-of-care immunoassay analyser with single-use assay cartridges (cardiac troponin I,
NT-proBNP, CRP, D-dimer). Firmware KS3-FW 4.2; companion software KS3-Link 2.1.

**Classification.** Class C under classification rule 3 (devices for detecting markers of acute cardiac events where
an erroneous result could lead to a life-threatening decision). Not class D: no transfusion, transplantation or
high-risk infectious-agent use. Classification rationale DOC-1003.

**Intended purpose.** Quantitative measurement in venous or capillary whole blood and plasma, by health
professionals (nurses, physicians, laboratory technicians) at the point of care: emergency departments, acute
medical units, GP practices and ambulance hubs. This is **near-patient testing** by professionals.

**What the Kestrel-3 is not.**
- Not a self-testing device: no lay-user operation is claimed; the IFU is written for professionals only.
- Not a companion diagnostic: no assay selects patients for a medicinal product.
- The "Kestrel-3 Home" concept studied by marketing in Q3 2026 (lay-user IFU draft DOC-1134, lay-user study
  protocol DOC-1161) is a separate possible future product. Its drafts sit in an uncontrolled concept folder and
  are not part of this submission.

**Configurations.** KS3-A (analyser, mains), KS3-B (analyser, battery dock), cartridge families C-TNI, C-BNP,
C-CRP, C-DDM; accessories listed in DOC-1004.

**Previous generation.** Kestrel-2 (certificate 2025-01-20, NB 2291). Kestrel-2 documents carry DOC-08xx numbers
and are archived; none of them is cited in the Kestrel-3 file.

Ossendrecht, R. Montoya. 1 Scope 1.1 This standard governs the table of contents (ToC) of every Orvane IVD technical file prepared for a notified body, the index of defined terms that accompanies it, the gap list and the readiness statement. 2 Records of source 2.1 Controlled documents live in the product's controlled document store (Drive folder ' Technical File (controlled)'). Each file's version history is its release record: one entry per revision, giving the revision label, whether the revision was released, routed for approval or is a working draft, its page count and its number of open content placeholders. 2.2 The Document Control Register (Monday board ' Document Control Register') records the approval status of each revision. 2.3 Change control (ServiceNow change requests) authorises releases into the controlled store. 2.4 The glossary register (Notion database ' Glossary Register') holds the defined terms, their status and the controlled document that defines each. 2.5 The controlled store and change control are updated as releases happen. The register is reconciled from closed change requests at the weekly register sync (QA-SOP-007 6.4). Exports, copies, chat messages and working drafts of any of these records are not records. 3 Section catalogue 3.1 The ToC has thirty sections, S01 to S30. The DHF master index (Confluence) gives, for each product, the controlled document number that satisfies each section. One document may satisfy more than one section. S01 Device description and specification - satisfied by the device description and specification S02 Intended purpose and indications - satisfied by the intended purpose statement S03 Classification rationale - lay-user performance study - satisfied by the lay-user performance study report S27 Companion diagnostic - medicinal product consultation - satisfied by the medicinal product authority consultation record S28 Batch verification by an EU reference laboratory - satisfied by the reference laboratory batch verification record S29 Post-market surveillance plan - satisfied by the post-market surveillance plan S30 Summary of safety and performance - satisfied by the summary of safety and performance 4 Rules for each ToC row 4.1 Document number: the controlled document number the DHF master index gives for the section. 4.2 Version: the version in force, written with the store's revision label (for example 'Rev C'). The version in force is the highest revision present in the controlled store that is approved. A revision is approved when (a) the register shows it as Approved, or (b) it was released into the store under a change request that change control shows closed as implemented; the register entry for such a release follows at the next sync. 4.3 A revision that the register shows as In approval or Draft, or that the store records as a working draft, is not approved, whatever its page count or content. A revision the store records as routed for approval is not approved until the register shows it as Approved (4.2(a)). 4.4 A revision whose approval the register records as withdrawn is not in force, whatever else records its release or its signatures. A withdrawal does not reinstate an earlier revision unless the register shows that revision as Approved again. 4.5 Pages: the page count the store records for the version in force. 4.6 Completeness, one of: 'Complete' - a version is in force and its store entry records 0 open placeholders; 'Gap' - no version is in force, or the version in force records one or more open placeholders; 'Not applicable' - section 5 excludes the section for the product. 4.7 Where no version is in force the row reads Version 'None in force', Pages 0, Completeness 'Gap'; the Document number is still given. 4.8 Not applicable rows read Document number 'N/A', Version 'N/A', Pages 0. 4.9 The file page total is the sum, over the distinct documents cited with a version in force, of the pages of that version. A document cited by more than one section counts once. Not applicable rows and rows with no version in force add nothing. 5 Applicability by device class and intended use S08 Instructions for use - lay user: self-testing devices only. S25 Near-patient testing - performance with intended users: devices intended for near-patient testing (use by health professionals outside a laboratory). S26 Self-testing - lay-user performance study: self-testing devices only. S27 Companion diagnostic - medicinal product consultation: companion diagnostics only. S28 Batch verification by an EU reference laboratory: class D devices only. S30 Summary of safety and performance: class C and class D devices (Edition 2 required it for class D only). All other sections: every device. 5.1 Near-patient testing by health professionals is not self-testing. Concept documents for a possible future self-test variant do not make S08 or S26 applicable to the product being filed. 6 Index of defined terms 6.1 The index has one entry per term that the glossary register shows as Active and whose source document is cited by at least one applicable section of the ToC. 6.2 Retired and Proposed terms are not indexed. A term whose source document is cited only by Not applicable sections, or by no section, is not indexed. A term is indexed whether or not the section citing its source document is a gap. 6.3 Entry title: ' |
| ', where Section is the lowest-numbered applicable section citing the source document. Example: 'Calibrator lot | S01 | DOC-1001'. 7 Gap list 7.1 One ticket in the product's Jira project for each section whose Completeness is Gap, raised once the ToC is complete. The ticket description opens with 'TF-GAP
' (for example 'TF-GAP S05') followed by the reason. pages' - C, G and N being the numbers of ToC rows by Completeness and P the file page total of 4.9. Definition.value: The lowest concentration of the measurand that the analyser reliably distinguishes from zero, expressed as the limit of detection.
The coefficient of variation of repeated measurements plotted across the measuring interval of each assay cartridge.
A batch of calibrator material manufactured under one batch record and assigned one set of target values.
The single-use test unit holding the reagents for one Kestrel-3 assay run; replaces the term reagent pack.
A circumstance in which a patient, user or other person is exposed to one or more hazards from the analyser or its results.
The weighing of the clinical benefit of a Kestrel-3 result against the residual risks that remain after all risk control measures.
A user action or lack of action that leads to a different result than intended by the manufacturer or expected by the user.
A health professional trained to operate the analyser at the point of care: nurse, physician or laboratory technician.
Testing performed outside a laboratory environment by a health professional, close to the patient.
The interval over which results are proportional to the concentration of the measurand within the stated deviation.
A substance in the sample other than the measurand that changes the measured result.
The period during which an unopened cartridge, stored as labelled, keeps its stated performance.
Any identifiable part of the Kestrel-3 embedded or companion software, at any level of decomposition.
The series of numeric or alphanumeric characters on the label that identifies the analyser or cartridge model and production unit.
The ability of the analyser to yield results correlated with a particular clinical condition in the target population.
The activities that collect and review experience with the Kestrel-3 placed on the market to identify any need for action.
A person without formal training in a relevant field of health care who performs a test at home.
A result produced and read by a lay user without professional supervision.
Former name of the single-use test unit; retired 2026-11-05 in favour of Cartridge.
Former term for the reportable range; retired 2026-10-22, the analytical reports now use linearity range.
Proposed term for the matrix that maps residual risk to acceptability; not yet adopted by the glossary board.

arguments.content:
Margit,

the Kestrel-3 ToC, the index of defined terms (16 entries) and the gap list are in place.
Rows: 23 Complete, 3 Gap (S16, S23, S29), 4 Not applicable (S08, S26, S27, S28). File page total 784 pages.

final_message:
Kestrel-3 technical file - ToC, term index, gap list and readiness statement are done (ORV-RA-STD-014 Edition 3).

Section counts by status: 23 Complete, 3 Gap, 4 Not applicable (the same figures as the readiness statement subject: "Kestrel-3 TF readiness: 23 complete, 3 gap, 4 not applicable, 784 pages").

What changed while I was working, and what it moved:
- After the ToC rows were written, the controlled store received new versions of two documents, released under change request CHG0041187 (closed as implemented): the risk management report DOC-1047 moved from Rev E (46 pages) to Rev F (52 pages), and the stability report DOC-1188 moved from Rev B (24 pages, open placeholders) to Rev C (31 pages, open placeholders 0).
- S13 (risk management report) now cites DOC-1047 Rev F, 52 pages, instead of Rev E (46 pages).
- S14 (benefit-risk determination) moved with it: S14 is satisfied by the same document DOC-1047, so it also cites Rev F, 52 pages.
- S22 (stability) now cites DOC-1188 Rev C (31 pages): Rev C closed the open placeholders of Rev B, so S22 is Complete instead of a gap and dropped off the gap list - 3 gaps remain where there would otherwise have been 4, and the Complete count is 23 instead of 22.
- The page total rose from 771 to 784 pages (+13) because of these two late releases.
- Why they count although the Document Control Register does not list them yet: STD-014 rule 4.2(b) and QA-SOP-007 6.4 accept a release under a change request closed as implemented as approval evidence until the weekly register sync; the 13 November sync was skipped and the next one is 20 November.
- Earlier in the run the approval of the professional IFU DOC-1133 Rev G completed (register and DocuSign envelope env-ks3-1133g, 2026-11-16T08:52); S07 therefore cites Rev G (68 pages) instead of Rev F (64 pages).

Versions used where the obvious choice was not the right one:
- S15 cites DOC-1102 Rev C (33 pages): Rev D is stored for its approval route but the register still shows it In approval, so it is not in force.
- S20 cites DOC-1111 Rev C (29 pages), released under the closed change request CHG0041102 on 12 November; the register still shows Rev B only because the sync has not run.
- S17 cites DOC-1074, the usability engineering file - not DOC-1047, the risk management report (the working draft had the transposed number).

Departures from Ines's working draft (each explained above or below): S07, S13, S14, S15, S16, S17, S20, S22, S25, S29, S30. The draft followed Edition 2 and the register export of 9 November.

Not applicable sections and why (STD-014 section 5; Kestrel-3 is class C, professional near-patient use, not self-testing, not a companion diagnostic):
- S08 Instructions for use - lay user: self-testing devices only.
- S26 Self-testing - lay-user performance study: self-testing devices only.
- S27 Companion diagnostic consultation: companion diagnostics only.
- S28 Batch verification by an EU reference laboratory: class D devices only.
- S25 (near-patient testing with intended users) stays applicable: near-patient testing by health professionals is not self-testing. S30 (summary of safety and performance) stays applicable: Edition 3 requires the SSP for class C as well as class D (Edition 2's class-D-only rule is superseded).

Remaining gaps and why each is a gap (one KTF ticket each):
- S16: DOC-1103 Rev C is approved and in force but its store entry records an open placeholder (penetration test annex).
- S23: DOC-1120 exists only as a working draft (Rev A); no version is in force.
- S29: the approval of DOC-1200 Rev A was withdrawn under CAPA-0912, so no PMS plan is in force (the DocuSign envelope still reads completed, but the register's withdrawal governs).

Page total method: 784 pages = the sum of the pages of each distinct document with a version in force (rule 4.9). DOC-1047 is cited by both S13 and S14 but counted once; Not applicable rows and the rows with no version in force add nothing.

Index of defined terms: 16 entries. Left out: Lay user (source DOC-1134 is not cited by any applicable section); Self-test result (source DOC-1161 is not cited by any applicable section); Reagent pack (status Retired); Measuring interval (status Retired); Residual risk acceptability matrix (status Proposed).

For document control to pick up: the register still needs to record DOC-1047 Rev F and DOC-1188 Rev C (released under CHG0041187) and DOC-1111 Rev C (CHG0041102) at the next sync. I did not approve, sign, route or re-status anything, and nothing was uploaded to the notified-body portal - the upload is yours after sign-off.
